portion_doctrine: Raw video transcripts (2 spliced interviews): product designer + John Galliano. Heavy storytelling flavor, light on tactical specificity. Mostly boilerplate generalist design philosophy. Signal-to-noise ratio: 15% (5 reusable methods, 95% narrative padding).
operating_rules: Emotional Cutting: Emotional intent is coded INTO garment construction itself, not applied afterward via styling. Identify emotional scenario > translate to physical gestures > cut fabric to preserve those gestures permanently. Fabric becomes silent actor; cutting is the script.

Movement + posture direction: Partner with movement director. Teach corset breathing via Pilates diaphragm placement. When models feel unstable, turn anxiety into choreography: 'hold broken pose, center yourself, breathe, take four steps, break again.' Converts unintended wobble into intentional shape.

Muse continuity protocol: Use same muses across all fittings, shoots, mood checks. They retain gestural memory from prior sessions and teach new models the tone/stance/walk. Non-verbal feedback: their body language signals what's wrong before they speak.

First-idea lock: When lost in iteration, return to the first idea. Second-guessing leads to over-refinement and lost original direction. First idea is correct because it holds the core intuition before doubt crept in.

Plan the meta, free the work: Plan TIME for research and objective-setting. Research itself must be uninhibited (books, markets, film, theater, flea markets). Separate meta-planning from creative execution; let creative work live in its own world without external interference.
content_ideas: How to embed narrative intent into construction (rather than styling as afterthought)
Movement direction as a design discipline (not just runway walk coaching)
Using constraint (corset, heel, broken pose) as creative material instead of problem to solve
Building institutional memory via repeated collaborators
weird_gold: Thomas immediately understood broken-doll pose before the outfit was even designed. He inhabited the character so completely that the team had to coach him OUT of it. Suggests: cast for emotional intelligence / character intuition BEFORE technical skill.

Galliano's narrative-building works backward from emotional scenario (muddy nighttime under bridge) to specific garment interventions (hem cut short to avoid puddles, cardigan rumpled to signal haste). Emotional geography creates design requirements.
Muse's reminders after 3-week fitting gaps suggest documentation system: keep motion-capture or video record of all fitting gestures so team remembers what they approved 3 weeks prior.
